items.q: Which national park is famous for its hoodoos?
items.f: On more than 170 nights a year, the temperature at Bryce swings above and below freezing. Water that freezes in cracks helps carve the hoodoos, a process called frost wedging.
items.s: National Park Service: Hoodoos

items.q: Which park's springs were set aside in 1832, making it the nation's oldest national reservation?
items.f: That was 40 years before Yellowstone became the first national park.
items.s: National Park Service: Yellowstone History FAQs

items.q: What was Gateway Arch National Park's former name?
items.f: The park covers 90.96 acres along the Mississippi River in St. Louis.
items.s: National Park Service: Gateway Arch History & Culture

items.q: What do you need to climb the cables to the top of Yosemite's Half Dome?
w: Nothing, it's first come, first served
items.f: There's a preseason lottery in March and daily lotteries during the season.
items.s: National Park Service: Half Dome Permits

items.q: Which national park has the lowest point in North America?
items.f: Badwater Basin is 282 feet below sea level, and its salt flats cover nearly 200 square miles.
items.s: National Park Service: Badwater Basin

items.q: Why isn't Bryce Canyon technically a canyon?
items.a: No river carved it. It's a series of amphitheaters.
w: It was made by a glacier
items.f: Rain and snowmelt eroded giant bowl-shaped amphitheaters filled with hoodoos.
items.s: National Park Service: Bryce Amphitheater

items.q: How much higher is the Grand Canyon's North Rim than the South Rim?
items.f: The North Rim is so high that snow usually closes its road from late fall to mid-May.
items.s: National Park Service: Grand Canyon FAQs

items.q: Badlands National Park is famous for what besides its striped buttes?
items.f: It has one of the world's richest fossil mammal beds. Fossils found there include ancient rhinos and saber-toothed cats.
items.s: National Park Service: Paleontology in the White River Badlands

items.q: Which is the smallest U.S. national park?
items.f: The St. Louis park covers about 91 acres.
items.s: National Park Service: Gateway Arch Nature

items.q: Which national park protects the world's longest known cave system?
items.f: Officially, more than 420 miles of passages have been mapped, and explorers are still finding more.
items.s: National Park Service: Additional Miles Added to Mammoth Cave

items.q: During the winter of 1971–72, how much snow fell at Paradise on Mount Rainier?
items.f: That's 93.5 feet. It held the world record for annual snowfall until 1998.
items.s: National Park Service: Mount Rainier Snowfall

items.q: Which park is often called the 'Galápagos of North America'?
items.f: The islands are home to 145 plant and animal species found nowhere else, including the island fox.
items.s: National Park Service: Island Fox

items.q: The Painted Wall, Colorado's tallest cliff, is in which national park?
items.f: The Painted Wall rises 2,250 feet from the river to the rim, and pale bands of pegmatite rock run across it.
items.s: National Park Service: Painted Wall Overlook

items.q: About how many miles of the Appalachian Trail run through Shenandoah National Park?
items.f: The whole trail runs about 2,175 miles from Georgia to Maine.
items.s: National Park Service: Appalachian Trail in Shenandoah

items.q: How tall is the Gateway Arch in St. Louis?
items.f: It's also 630 feet wide at the base. The arch is the tallest human-built monument in the U.S.
items.s: National Park Service: Gateway Arch

items.q: In which national park do alligators and crocodiles live side by side?
items.f: South Florida is the only place where America's two native crocodilian species live together.
items.s: National Park Service: American Crocodile

items.q: The Hoh Rain Forest is in which national park?
items.f: The Hoh gets an average of about 140 inches of rain a year.
items.s: National Park Service: Visiting the Hoh Rain Forest

items.q: About how many miles of wild Pacific coastline does Olympic National Park protect?
items.f: Most of the coast can only be reached on foot, and overnight hikers need a permit.
items.s: National Park Service: Olympic Coast

items.q: Which scenic road runs the full length of Shenandoah National Park?
items.f: The drive runs 105 miles along the crest of the Blue Ridge Mountains, and it's the park's only public road.
items.s: National Park Service: Driving Skyline Drive

items.q: Kings Canyon is the deepest canyon in which mountain range?
items.f: The Cedar Grove area sits at the heart of the canyon.
items.s: National Park Service: Kings Canyon

items.q: Which future president ranched in the North Dakota badlands in the 1880s and now has a national park named for him?
items.f: His Maltese Cross Cabin is on display at the park's South Unit Visitor Center.
items.s: National Park Service: Maltese Cross Cabin

items.q: Which two rivers divide Canyonlands National Park into its districts?
w: The San Juan and the Virgin
items.f: No roads cross the rivers inside the park, so driving between districts can take 2 to 6 hours.
items.s: National Park Service: Canyonlands Places to Go

items.q: Which California national park has examples of all four main types of volcanoes?
items.f: Lassen Peak itself is one of the largest plug dome volcanoes in the world.
items.s: National Park Service: Lassen Volcanoes

items.q: Which is the only U.S. national park south of the equator?
items.f: The park protects tropical rainforest and Indo-Pacific coral reefs.
items.s: National Park Service: American Samoa Fact Sheet

items.q: The highest point in Texas is in which national park?
items.f: Guadalupe Peak rises to 8,751 feet. The round-trip hike to the top is 8.4 miles and climbs 3,000 feet.
items.s: National Park Service: Guadalupe Peak

items.q: In 1995, only about how many Florida panthers were left in the wild?
items.f: A genetic rescue program helped, and in 2020 South Florida had an estimated 120 to 230.
items.s: National Park Service: Florida Panther

items.q: Which endangered animal was reintroduced to Badlands National Park in 1994?
items.f: By the mid-1980s only 18 were left in the world. All of them were taken into captive breeding.
items.s: National Park Service: Black-footed Ferret

items.q: Ohio's Brandywine Falls is in which national park?
items.f: A boardwalk leads to views of the falls tumbling into Brandywine Gorge.
items.s: National Park Service: Brandywine Falls

items.q: What happens on Medano Creek at Great Sand Dunes in late spring?
items.a: It flows in waves, like a beach
items.f: Tiny sand dams build up and break about every 20 seconds, sending small 'surge' waves down the creek.
items.s: National Park Service: Medano Creek

items.q: In 1991, a 60-foot slab of rock fell from which famous arch in Arches National Park?
items.f: Hikers caught it on video. The trail under the arch has been closed ever since.
items.s: National Park Service: 1991 Landscape Arch Rock Fall

items.q: Which South Carolina national park protects old-growth bottomland hardwood forest and has synchronous fireflies?
items.f: The synchronous fireflies, Photuris frontalis, usually put on their show for about two weeks between mid-May and early June.
items.s: National Park Service: Synchronous Fireflies at Congaree

items.q: How did Olympic National Park's Hurricane Ridge get its name?
items.a: From its winds, which can gust over 75 mph
items.f: The ridge sits at about 5,242 feet and has sweeping views of the Olympic Mountains.
items.s: National Park Service: Hurricane Ridge Brochure

items.q: Carlsbad Caverns' Big Room is the largest what in North America?
items.f: Its floor covers about 8.2 acres, and a self-guided trail loops around it.
items.s: National Park Service: Carlsbad Cavern

items.q: How tall is North America's highest peak, in Denali National Park?
items.f: In 2025 the peak's official name went back to Mount McKinley, but the park is still called Denali National Park and Preserve.
items.s: National Park Service: Mountain Name Origins

items.q: Which Yosemite waterfall can glow orange like a 'firefall' at sunset in February?
items.f: It only happens on clear evenings when the seasonal fall on El Capitan is flowing and the sun hits it just right.
items.s: National Park Service: Horsetail Fall

items.q: At which Utah national park can you pick fruit from historic orchards?
items.f: You can eat ripe fruit in the Fruita orchards for free. Fruit you take with you is paid for at a self-pay station.
items.s: National Park Service: Capitol Reef Orchards

items.q: In 2024, the Smokies' highest peak, Clingmans Dome, officially regained which Cherokee name?
items.f: The Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians led the effort. The peak is 6,643 feet tall.
items.s: National Park Service: Ancient Name Returns

items.q: Fat Bear Week celebrates the brown bears of which national park?
items.f: Fat Bear Week started in 2014. The bears fatten up on salmon at Brooks Falls before winter.
items.s: National Park Service: Fat Bear Week

items.q: Since 2022, what do you need to hike the final chained section of Zion's Angels Landing?
items.f: Without a permit you can still hike as far as Scout Lookout.
items.s: National Park Service: Angels Landing Permits

items.q: Cliff Palace, North America's largest cliff dwelling, is in which park?
items.f: Ancestral Puebloan people built Cliff Palace with about 150 rooms.
items.s: National Park Service: Cliff Palace

items.q: In 1864, Lincoln protected Yosemite Valley and which sequoia grove?
items.f: The grove has more than 500 mature giant sequoias, including the Grizzly Giant.
items.s: National Park Service: Mariposa Grove

items.q: When is the best time to hear Acadia's Thunder Hole boom?
items.a: One to two hours before high tide
items.f: Waves trap air in a small cave, and when it bursts out, spray can shoot more than 40 feet high.
items.s: National Park Service: Thunder Hole

items.q: In Sequoia National Park, what can you drive through on Crescent Meadow Road?
items.f: The tree fell in 1937, and a tunnel was cut through it the next year. Taller vehicles use a bypass.
items.s: National Park Service: Tunnel Log

items.q: How are supplies carried down to Phantom Ranch at the bottom of the Grand Canyon?
items.f: Mule trains also pack supplies for trail crews and ranger stations deep in the canyon.
items.s: National Park Service: Mule Trips

items.q: Which Alaska national park has the largest active sand dune field in arctic North America?
items.f: Caribou herds cross the Great Kobuk Sand Dunes on their spring and fall migrations.
items.s: National Park Service: Great Kobuk Sand Dunes

items.q: Theodore Roosevelt National Park's South Unit is home to herds of which animal?
items.f: They descend from ranch horses that escaped or were let go, and the park manages them as part of its history.
items.s: National Park Service: Horses

items.q: Marjory Stoneman Douglas's famous 1947 book called the Everglades what?
items.f: Everglades National Park was dedicated later that same year, in December 1947.
items.s: National Park Service: Marjory Stoneman Douglas

items.q: The rainwater that comes out of Hot Springs National Park's springs fell about how long ago?
items.f: It sinks deep underground, heats up and comes back out at about 143°F.
items.s: National Park Service: Hot Springs Geology

items.q: Hyperion, the tallest known tree in the world, grows in which park?
items.f: Hyperion is deep off-trail. Hikers trying to reach it have trampled the plants around it, so the park asks people not to go.
items.s: National Park Service: Should I Hike to Hyperion?

items.q: Which national park has the deepest lake in the United States?
items.f: Crater Lake is 1,943 feet deep. It fills the caldera left when Mount Mazama erupted about 7,700 years ago.
items.s: National Park Service: Crater Lake

items.q: Which park has more glaciers than any other U.S. protected area outside Alaska?
items.f: The park holds about a quarter of all the glaciers in the lower 48 states.
items.s: National Park Service: North Cascades Glaciers

items.q: How tall is the Grand Teton?
items.f: Elevations in the park range from about 6,320 feet on the valley floor to the Grand Teton's summit.
items.s: National Park Service: Grand Teton Nature

items.q: Which California park, known for its endangered condors, became a national park in 2013?
items.f: Pinnacles was the 59th national park, and it helps reintroduce California condors to the wild.
items.s: National Park Service: Pinnacles Present Day

items.q: In what year was the National Park Service created?
items.f: Woodrow Wilson signed the Organic Act on August 25, 1916, and the NPS celebrates that date as its birthday. Stephen Mather was its first director.
items.s: National Park Service: Creation of the National Park Service

items.q: Cuyahoga Valley National Park is in which state?
items.f: The Cuyahoga Valley Scenic Railroad runs 26 miles through the park.
items.s: National Park Service: Scenic Train Ride

items.q: Which national park is the only one with a stretch of historic Route 66?
items.f: A 1932 Studebaker marks the spot where Route 66 once crossed the park.
items.s: National Park Service: Route 66 Pullout

items.q: About how many steps climb to the top of Sequoia's Moro Rock?
items.f: The historic staircase climbs about 300 feet to a granite summit with huge views.
items.s: National Park Service: Moro Rock

items.q: What is the most glaciated peak in the contiguous United States?
items.f: Rainier has 28 named glaciers, which cover about 35 square miles.
items.s: National Park Service: Mount Rainier Press Kit

items.q: Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park includes part of which volcano, the largest active volcano on Earth?
items.f: Mauna Loa rises 13,681 feet above sea level, plus about 30,000 feet more below the sea.
items.s: National Park Service: Mauna Loa

items.q: What is the highest point on Trail Ridge Road in Rocky Mountain National Park?
items.f: The road runs 48 miles between Estes Park and Grand Lake.
items.s: National Park Service: Trail Ridge Road

items.q: According to legend, Mormon pioneers named the Joshua tree after its branches looked like what?
items.f: The NPS notes the story isn't backed by records, so it may be more myth than history.
items.s: National Park Service: Joshua Trees

items.q: Mammoth Cave is home to fish that have no what?
items.f: In total darkness, eyes aren't useful, so these cavefish don't grow them. They're also pale and pinkish.
items.s: National Park Service: Mammoth Cave Fish

items.q: Which island park in Lake Superior is home to the world's longest-running predator-prey study?
items.f: Scientists have studied the island's wolves and moose since 1958.
items.s: National Park Service: Wolves, an Ecological Study

items.q: Isle Royale National Park closes to all visitors during what part of the year?
items.f: Lake Superior's winter weather makes the island unsafe. Only wolf and moose researchers stay through the winter.
items.s: National Park Service: Isle Royale Hours and Seasons

items.q: About 40% of which Minnesota national park is water?
items.f: Houseboats are a popular way to explore it. They're rented from outfitters just outside the park.
items.s: National Park Service: Houseboating in Voyageurs

items.q: Wind Cave has more of which rare honeycomb-like cave formation than all other caves combined?
items.f: Boxwork is made of thin calcite fins that stick out from the cave walls and ceilings.
items.s: National Park Service: Wind Cave Speleothems

items.q: The highest peak in the contiguous United States sits on the edge of which national park?
items.f: Mount Whitney rises to 14,505 feet on the park's eastern boundary.
items.s: National Park Service: Mt. Whitney

items.q: Which granite wall rises more than 3,000 feet above Yosemite Valley?
items.f: El Capitan is a favorite climb for experienced rock climbers.
items.s: National Park Service: Rock Formations in Yosemite Valley

items.q: Fort Jefferson, a huge 1800s brick fort, is in which national park?
items.f: The park is almost 70 miles west of Key West, and the only way in is by boat or seaplane.
items.s: National Park Service: Dry Tortugas Directions

items.q: Which park, on Lake Michigan, became the 61st national park in 2019?
items.f: It had been Indiana Dunes National Lakeshore since 1966.
items.s: National Park Service: Indiana Dunes FAQs

items.q: How far does Yosemite Falls drop in total?
items.f: It falls in three sections: the 1,430-foot upper fall, 675 feet of middle cascades, and the 320-foot lower fall.
items.s: National Park Service: Yosemite Waterfalls

items.q: Who built Acadia's 45 miles of car-free carriage roads?
items.f: He built them between 1913 and 1940 and paid for 16 of the 17 stone-faced bridges.
items.s: National Park Service: Acadia Carriage Roads

items.q: Which is the only national park with working sled dogs?
items.f: The kennels started in 1922, and the dogs still patrol the park's wilderness in winter.
items.s: National Park Service: Denali Kennels

items.q: Which giant sequoia was named 'the Nation's Christmas Tree' in 1926?
items.f: It grows in Grant Grove in Kings Canyon National Park, and people still hike to it every December.
items.s: National Park Service: The General Grant Tree

items.q: Since about 1750, Glacier Bay's ice has retreated roughly how far?
items.f: When Captain Vancouver's crew passed in 1794, the bay was just a small dent in a huge glacier.
items.s: National Park Service: Glacier Bay's Glacial History

items.q: In 1978, Mesa Verde and which other park became the first U.S. World Heritage Sites?
items.f: Mesa Verde was recognized for its Ancestral Pueblo cliff dwellings, and Yellowstone for its geysers and wildlife.
items.s: National Park Service: Mesa Verde World Heritage

items.q: From October 7 to March 6, which Acadia summit is the first place in the U.S. to see the sunrise?
items.f: The summit is very popular, so arrive about an hour before sunrise.
items.s: National Park Service: Cadillac Mountain

items.q: Which two deserts meet in Joshua Tree National Park?
items.f: Joshua trees grow in the higher, cooler Mojave part of the park, while the Colorado Desert lies below 3,000 feet.
items.s: National Park Service: Joshua Tree Map and Brochure

items.q: What is the highest peak in Rocky Mountain National Park?
items.f: At 14,259 feet, the Keyhole Route to its top is a long, exposed climb, not a simple hike.
items.s: National Park Service: Longs Peak

items.q: Which national park has more than 2,000 documented natural stone arches?
items.f: The park has the densest concentration of natural stone arches in the world. The longest, Landscape Arch, spans 306 feet.
items.s: National Park Service: Arches

items.q: Which national park gets the most visitors?
items.f: It recorded more than 12 million recreational visits in 2024. There's no entrance fee, but you need a parking tag.
items.s: National Park Service: Great Smoky Mountains Park Statistics

items.q: Exit Glacier, the only glacier you can drive to in Kenai Fjords, flows from which icefield?
items.f: The Harding Icefield and its glaciers cover about 700 square miles, and at least 38 glaciers flow out of it.
items.s: National Park Service: The Harding Icefield

items.q: What makes the 'sailing stones' slide across Death Valley's Racetrack Playa?
items.a: Thin sheets of ice pushed by wind
items.f: Scientists first watched it happen in 2014. Some rocks weigh up to 700 pounds.
items.s: National Park Service: Sailing Stones

items.q: Which national park has the tallest sand dunes in North America?
items.f: Star Dune and Hidden Dune are tied for tallest at about 741 feet. The park is in Colorado.
items.s: National Park Service: Star Dune

items.q: White Sands National Park's dunes are made of what?
items.f: The park protects much of the world's largest gypsum dunefield, which covers about 275 square miles.
items.s: National Park Service: White Sands

items.q: How many historic bathhouses line Bathhouse Row in Hot Springs National Park?
items.f: The Buckstaff is the only one that has run continuously for over a century.
items.s: National Park Service: Bathhouse Row Today

items.q: About 95% of which Florida national park is water?
items.f: To see most of the park beyond the visitor center, you need a boat.
items.s: National Park Service: Biscayne National Park

items.q: Great Basin National Park protects groves of which extremely old trees?
items.f: A bristlecone named Prometheus, cut down in 1964, had 4,862 growth rings.
items.s: National Park Service: The Prometheus Story

items.q: Dr. Samuel Mudd, convicted after Lincoln's assassination, was imprisoned at which national park fort?
items.f: During an 1867 yellow fever outbreak, Mudd cared for sick soldiers and prisoners. He was pardoned in 1869.
items.s: National Park Service: Dr. Samuel Mudd

items.q: In 1932, Glacier and Canada's Waterton Lakes together became the world's first what?
items.f: The two parks were later named a joint World Heritage Site in 1995.
items.s: National Park Service: Glacier International Designations

items.q: The General Sherman Tree, the largest tree on Earth by volume, is in which park?
items.f: General Sherman is about 275 feet tall. The latest estimate puts its age at about 2,200 years.
items.s: National Park Service: The General Sherman Tree

items.q: Which was the first national park created to protect a cave?
items.f: Theodore Roosevelt signed the bill on January 9, 1903, making Wind Cave the eighth national park.
items.s: National Park Service: A National Park is Created

items.q: Which West Virginia park became a national park in December 2020?
items.f: It had been a unit of the park system since 1978, when it was designated New River Gorge National River.
items.s: National Park Service: New River Gorge is Now a National Park

items.q: Before Zion became a national park in 1919, what was it called?
items.f: The canyon became a national monument in 1909, and Congress made it Zion National Park on November 19, 1919.
items.s: National Park Service: Zion People

items.q: What is the 'Old Man of the Lake' at Crater Lake?
items.a: A tree trunk that has floated upright for over 100 years
w: A rock island shaped like a face
items.f: The 30-foot hemlock log was first recorded in 1896 and drifts around the lake on the wind.
items.s: National Park Service: The Old Man

items.q: Which river carved the Grand Canyon?
items.f: The Colorado River runs 277 river miles through the canyon.
items.s: National Park Service: Grand Canyon Geology

items.q: Lassen Volcanic became a national park in 1916, soon after its peak did what?
items.f: Lassen Peak's biggest blast came in May 1915.
items.s: National Park Service: Lassen Park Significance

items.q: For how many miles does the Rio Grande form Big Bend National Park's southern boundary?
items.f: The river's big southward curve through the area gives the park its name.
items.s: National Park Service: The Rio Grande

items.q: Which Alaska national park has no roads, trails or campgrounds at all?
items.f: Most visitors fly in on small planes with floats or tundra tires. Experienced hikers count six miles as a good day.
items.s: National Park Service: Gates of the Arctic

items.q: Who is often called the 'Father of the National Parks'?
items.f: Muir's writing helped start a national conservation movement. He also helped create the Sierra Club in 1892.
items.s: National Park Service: National Park Service Remembers John Muir

items.q: Petrified Forest's fossil logs date to which era of Earth's history?
items.a: The Late Triassic, more than 200 million years ago
items.f: The trees fell into ancient rivers about 216 million years ago, then slowly turned to stone.
items.s: National Park Service: Giant Logs

items.q: Haleakalā National Park is on which Hawaiian island?
items.f: The summit is 10,023 feet high, and you need a reservation to watch the sunrise from the top.
items.s: National Park Service: Haleakalā Geology

items.q: In Hawaiian tradition, the volcano goddess Pele is said to live in which crater?
items.f: It sits in Kīlauea's summit caldera in Hawaiʻi Volcanoes. Many people still leave offerings there.
items.s: National Park Service: Pele

items.q: Death Valley holds the world record for the hottest air temperature ever measured. What was it?
items.f: It was recorded at Furnace Creek on July 10, 1913.
items.s: National Park Service: Death Valley Weather

items.q: At Saguaro National Park, about how old is a saguaro cactus when it grows its first arm?
items.f: In drier spots, it can take 100 years for a saguaro to grow an arm.
items.s: National Park Service: Saguaro Arms Project

items.q: Which is the largest U.S. national park?
items.f: At about 13.2 million acres, it's roughly the size of six Yellowstones.
items.s: National Park Service: Wrangell–St. Elias

items.q: At Carlsbad Caverns, visitors gather on summer evenings to watch which animals fly out of the cave?
items.f: Rangers hold a free Bat Flight Program at the cave's Natural Entrance. Cameras and other electronics aren't allowed, to protect the bats.
items.s: National Park Service: Bat Flight Program

items.q: Great Smoky Mountains National Park is nicknamed the world capital of which animal?
items.f: The park has more salamander species than any other place on Earth, including the red-cheeked salamander, which lives nowhere else.
items.s: National Park Service: Great Smoky Mountains FAQs

items.q: Capitol Reef's Waterpocket Fold is a nearly 100-mile-long what?
items.f: It's one of the longest exposed monoclines in the world, a giant step in the rock layers.
items.s: National Park Service: Capitol Reef Geology

items.q: Alaska's Kennecott, inside Wrangell–St. Elias, is a historic mill town for mining which metal?
items.f: From 1911 to 1938, nearly $200 million worth of copper was processed in its 14-story mill.
items.s: National Park Service: Kennecott Mines

items.q: Which president is NOT carved into Mount Rushmore?
items.f: The sculptor chose Washington, Jefferson, Theodore Roosevelt and Lincoln to represent the nation's birth, growth, development and preservation.
items.s: National Park Service: Why These Four Presidents?

items.q: How did Death Valley's Badwater Basin get its name, according to a popular story?
items.a: A surveyor's mule refused to drink the water
w: A flood ruined a town there
items.f: The water isn't poisonous, just very salty.
items.s: National Park Service: Badwater Basin

items.q: The observation tower on Kuwohi (formerly Clingmans Dome) was built in what year?
items.f: The 45-foot tower has a 375-foot spiral ramp to the top.
items.s: National Park Service: Kuwohi Observation Tower

items.q: Which animal appears on the National Park Service arrowhead logo?
items.f: The bison stands for all the wildlife the parks protect.
items.s: National Park Service: History of the NPS Arrowhead

items.q: Which of these is a national memorial, not a national park?
items.f: The National Park Service runs it, but it's officially a national memorial.
items.s: National Park Service: Mount Rushmore National Memorial

items.q: How tall is the opening under Delicate Arch?
items.f: It's the largest free-standing arch in Arches National Park.
items.s: National Park Service: Delicate Arch

items.q: Which very popular national park charges no entrance fee?
items.f: A 1951 agreement bars tolls on its main roads, but cars parked more than 15 minutes need a parking tag.
items.s: National Park Service: Why No Entrance Fee?

items.q: About how big is Gates of the Arctic National Park, which has no trails at all?
items.f: Experienced hikers count six miles as a good day there.
items.s: National Park Service: Gates of the Arctic

items.q: Which famous arch is a widely recognized symbol of Utah?
items.f: The 3-mile round-trip hike to it climbs about 480 feet.
items.s: National Park Service: Delicate Arch

items.q: What is the most famous tree in Yosemite's Mariposa Grove?
items.f: The giant sequoia is 209 feet tall and about 1,800 years old.
items.s: National Park Service: Mariposa Grove

items.q: What do kids usually earn for finishing a park's Junior Ranger activity book?
items.f: Most parks give the booklets out free at visitor centers, and many let you download them.
items.s: National Park Service: Junior Ranger Programs

items.q: Who was the first guardian of Yosemite after Lincoln protected it in 1864?
items.f: He held the job for 24 years.
items.s: National Park Service: Explorers and Recorders

items.q: Grand Canyon National Park is in which state?
items.f: The Colorado River carved the canyon, which is about a mile deep in places.
items.s: National Park Service: Grand Canyon

items.q: Acadia National Park is in which state?
items.f: Most of the park is on Mount Desert Island, along the Atlantic coast.
items.s: National Park Service: Acadia

items.q: At its deepest, the Grand Canyon is about how deep?
items.f: It's 277 river miles long.
items.s: National Park Service: Grand Canyon FAQs

items.q: About how many sockeye salmon jump Brooks Falls in Katmai each year?
items.f: That's why so many brown bears gather at the falls in July.
items.s: National Park Service: The Bears of Brooks River

items.q: What kind of tree is on the National Park Service arrowhead logo?
items.f: The tree stands for plants. Mountains and water stand for scenery and recreation, and the arrowhead shape for history.
items.s: National Park Service: History of the NPS Arrowhead
